name: Grade 6 T3: micro:bit Programming Projects
description: micro:bit parts, inputs, outputs, LED display, buttons, variables, sensors, conditions, and final project explanations.

words.definition: A small programmable computer used to learn inputs, outputs, sensors, and code.
words.example: The micro:bit showed an icon on its LED display.

words.definition: A block-based programming tool used to create micro:bit programs.
words.example: The student opened MakeCode to build a button program.

words.definition: A digital version of a device used to test a program on the screen.
words.example: The simulator showed how the micro:bit would react.

words.definition: Information a computer receives from a button, sensor, or user action.
words.example: Pressing button A was the input.

words.definition: What a computer shows, plays, or does after code runs.
words.example: The output was a smile icon on the LED display.

words.definition: A small light that can turn on or off in a pattern.
words.example: The micro:bit uses LEDs to show icons and text.

words.definition: A screen or set of lights that shows information.
words.example: The LED display showed the current counter value.

words.definition: A part that can be pressed to give input.
words.example: Button A increased the counter.

words.definition: A movement, such as shaking or tilting, used as an input.
words.example: The shake gesture started the program.

words.definition: A part that detects information from the environment.
words.example: The light sensor detected whether the room was bright.

words.definition: Brightness that a sensor can detect.
words.example: The program reacted when the light level was low.

words.definition: How hot or cold something is.
words.example: The temperature input changed the icon shown.

words.definition: A sensor that detects movement, tilting, or shaking.
words.example: The accelerometer noticed when the micro:bit was shaken.

words.definition: A sensor that can detect direction.
words.example: The compass can help a program know which way the micro:bit faces.

words.definition: A connection point on a micro:bit for input or output.
words.example: A pin can connect the micro:bit to another component.

words.definition: A named place in a program that stores a value that can change.
words.example: The variable stored the counter number.

words.definition: The number or information stored in a variable.
words.example: The counter value started at 0.

words.definition: To make a number larger.
words.example: Button A increased the score by 1.

words.definition: To make a number smaller.
words.example: Button B decreased the counter.

words.definition: To return something to its starting value or condition.
words.example: The reset button changed the counter back to 0.

words.definition: A rule or test that can be true or false.
words.example: The condition checked if the light level was below 50.

words.definition: A way to describe a condition and the action that happens when it is true.
words.example: If it is dark, then show a moon icon.

words.definition: A diagram that shows the steps and decisions in a program.
words.example: The flowchart showed the true and false outputs.

words.definition: A small picture or symbol shown on a screen or display.
words.example: The micro:bit displayed a heart icon.

words.definition: Text or information shown or sent by a program.
words.example: The program displayed the message Hello.

words.definition: A program or variable that keeps track of a changing number.
words.example: The counter increased each time the button was pressed.

words.definition: Able to respond to a user's actions or inputs.
words.example: The final micro:bit project was interactive because it reacted to buttons.

words.definition: To show how something works and explain it.
words.example: Students demonstrated their final micro:bit projects.
